name: constructor-research-mcp

tools.name: build_image
tools.description: Build a disk Dockerfile. IDs are generated automatically; omit build storage for the default. Waits up to wait_seconds (default 20), then continues in the background. Check get_deployment for the result. The Dockerfile rules in deploy_app apply.

ephemeral_build_disk_size_gb.description: Omit to use the API default (50 GB). Overrides must be 10–1000 GB.

request_id.description: Optional retry key. Omit it: the MCP generates deployment IDs automatically.

wait_seconds.description: Wait up to this many seconds for completion; execution continues in the MCP after the response.

desk_url.description: Link to the Constructor desk the user copied from the browser, e.g. https://constructor.app/research/projects/<project>/desks/<desk>/viewer/file. Supplies project_id and desk_id; ask the user for it instead of choosing a project or desk yourself.

tools.name: list_images
tools.description: List images with native build statuses and Dockerfile paths. Optionally filter by disk. Compact results by default; detailed=true returns full image records.

desk_url.description: Link to the Constructor desk the user copied from the browser, e.g. https://constructor.app/research/projects/<project>/desks/<desk>/viewer/file. Supplies project_id and desk_id; ask the user for it instead of choosing a project or desk yourself.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List files and folders on a project disk (the Constructor desk's project folder). Non-recursive by default; recursive=true walks subfolders up to max_entries.

path.description: Folder on the disk; '' is the root.

desk_url.description: Link to the Constructor desk the user copied from the browser, e.g. https://constructor.app/research/projects/<project>/desks/<desk>/viewer/file. Supplies project_id and desk_id; ask the user for it instead of choosing a project or desk yourself.

tools.name: create_folder
tools.description: Create a folder on a project disk, including missing parent folders. Existing folders are left unchanged.

path.description: Folder to create; missing parent folders are created too.

desk_url.description: Link to the Constructor desk the user copied from the browser, e.g. https://constructor.app/research/projects/<project>/desks/<desk>/viewer/file. Supplies project_id and desk_id; ask the user for it instead of choosing a project or desk yourself.

tools.name: sync_files
tools.description: Upload a local file or folder to a project disk. Compares by size and SHA-256 and sends only new and changed files; never deletes. New files and folders upload without asking. If existing files would be replaced, nothing is uploaded and status is confirm_required: ask the user once for the whole list, then repeat with confirm=true. dry_run=true only previews. Skips .git, node_modules, .env, .venv, __pycache__, .DS_Store and files over 100 MB. If the result is in_progress, repeat the same call to continue.

local_path.description: Absolute local file or folder. A folder's contents go into remote_path.

remote_path.description: Destination folder on the disk; '' is the root.

exclude.description: Extra names or '*' patterns to skip, matched against file names and relative paths.

dry_run.description: true only reports the plan, without uploading.

confirm.description: Needed only when existing files would be replaced: the first call returns the list for the user to approve once; repeat with confirm=true.

desk_url.description: Link to the Constructor desk the user copied from the browser, e.g. https://constructor.app/research/projects/<project>/desks/<desk>/viewer/file. Supplies project_id and desk_id; ask the user for it instead of choosing a project or desk yourself.

tools.name: move_path
tools.description: Rename or move files/folders on a project disk. Send every move for the request in one call: without confirm it returns the list (confirm_required) for the user to approve once; repeat with confirm=true. Never overwrites; the destination parent folder must exist.

to.description: New path. Its parent folder must exist; an existing target is never overwritten.

moves.description: All renames/moves for this request, approved together.

confirm.description: false (default) returns the full list for the user to approve once; true performs it.

desk_url.description: Link to the Constructor desk the user copied from the browser, e.g. https://constructor.app/research/projects/<project>/desks/<desk>/viewer/file. Supplies project_id and desk_id; ask the user for it instead of choosing a project or desk yourself.

tools.name: delete_path
tools.description: Delete files/folders (folders with all contents) on a project disk. Send every path for the request in one call: without confirm it returns what would be deleted (confirm_required) for the user to approve once; repeat with confirm=true. Cannot be undone.

paths.description: All files/folders to delete for this request, approved together. Folders are deleted with all contents.

confirm.description: false (default) returns the full list for the user to approve once; true performs it.

desk_url.description: Link to the Constructor desk the user copied from the browser, e.g. https://constructor.app/research/projects/<project>/desks/<desk>/viewer/file. Supplies project_id and desk_id; ask the user for it instead of choosing a project or desk yourself.

tools.name: deploy_app
tools.description: Deploy the WHOLE app in one request: prepare project/disk, build or reuse all images, resolve internal/public service references, configure and start. Runs in the background. IDs are automatic. To resume a failure, send deployment_id and service overrides (for example replacement image_id); successful builds are preserved. On failure, failure.log_tail and get_logs show what the build or service printed. Dockerfile rules: one Dockerfile per service named Dockerfile or <name>.dockerfile; docker-compose is not supported. The Dockerfile must build everything itself; no separate setup script the user runs before the build. The app listens on 0.0.0.0 on a fixed port; only one port per service can be public. Services reach each other through internal references (bare host:port by default, http:// only when scheme is set), never localhost; do not bake compose-style fallback hosts (http://db:5432) into ENV. Files uploaded to a desk lose the executable bit: RUN chmod 0755 any entrypoint script you COPY. In nginx configs use only the IPv4 listen line. A volume belongs to one service; services cannot share a volume. Volume data survives restarts and image changes but is wiped if the service is deleted or the volume is removed or changed. The build context is the folder containing the Dockerfile, exactly like a local docker build in that folder. Test the image locally (docker build/run) before uploading.

desk_url.description: Desk link from the user: sets project_id and the desk for builds without desk_id.

dockerfile.description: Disk path of the Dockerfile. With local_path: path inside that folder (default Dockerfile).

local_path.description: Local folder with the source and Dockerfile. The MCP uploads it to the disk first (new files without asking; replacing files needs confirm=true), then builds. Files matched by the folder's .dockerignore are not uploaded. A large folder may take several calls: on in_progress repeat the same deploy/update call.

remote_path.description: Disk folder for local_path; defaults to the local folder's name.

ephemeral_build_disk_size_gb.description: Omit to use the API default (50 GB). Overrides must be 10–1000 GB.

hardware.description: Omit this: the default hardware is used, and existing services keep theirs. Set it only when the app clearly cannot run on the default (needs a GPU, or loads large models/datasets into memory). Values are minimums; the smallest available option that meets them is chosen. get_deployment with desk_url lists hardware_options.

items.description: Persistent disk for this service only (see the volume rules). Changing name, mount_point or size_gb wipes it. On update, omit volumes to keep them; a supplied list replaces the current one.

environment_variables.description: Plain strings, or {service, port[, scheme]} to point at another service of the same app; never localhost.

scheme.description: Internal only: prefix added to the address. Omit it to get a bare host:port (for gRPC, databases, Temporal and similar); set http for an HTTP URL.

anyOf.description: Resolved by the MCP into the other service's address. internal: <host>:<port> inside the app (port required), e.g. svc-api.app-1234abcd.svc.cluster.local:7233, or http://... when scheme is set. public: the service's https URL.

confirm.description: Set after the user approved replacing existing disk files listed by a previous confirm_required response.

confirm_volume_wipe.description: Set only after the user approved losing the data in the volumes listed by a previous confirm_required response.

request_id.description: Optional retry key. Omit it: the MCP generates deployment IDs automatically.

wait_seconds.description: Wait up to this many seconds for completion; execution continues in the MCP after the response.

tools.name: update_app
tools.description: Update/add selected services in one request; preserve omitted settings. MCP handles builds, links and restarts in the background. Environment variables merge; supplied port/volume lists replace their lists. Resume a failed update using deployment_id and service overrides. The Dockerfile rules in deploy_app apply.

tools.name: start_app
tools.description: Start all or selected services as one operation. MCP handles all requests. Waits up to wait_seconds (default 20); remaining execution continues in the background. Started does not mean ready.

wait_seconds.description: Wait up to this many seconds for completion; execution continues in the MCP after the response.

desk_url.description: Link to the Constructor desk the user copied from the browser, e.g. https://constructor.app/research/projects/<project>/desks/<desk>/viewer/file. Supplies project_id and desk_id; ask the user for it instead of choosing a project or desk yourself.

tools.name: stop_app
tools.description: Stop all or selected services as one operation. MCP handles all requests. Waits up to wait_seconds (default 20). Stopped means stop requests accepted, not verified teardown.

wait_seconds.description: Wait up to this many seconds for completion; execution continues in the MCP after the response.

desk_url.description: Link to the Constructor desk the user copied from the browser, e.g. https://constructor.app/research/projects/<project>/desks/<desk>/viewer/file. Supplies project_id and desk_id; ask the user for it instead of choosing a project or desk yourself.

tools.name: get_deployment
tools.description: With deployment_id, observe/wait for background execution; the MCP owns execution. Each call waits up to wait_seconds (max 20); to wait longer, call again, as often as needed (a loop of get_deployment calls is fine), until execution is finished; do not answer the user while it is still in the background. Services carry status_changes and restarts_seen when the MCP saw the status change or a new container start. After sync_files (or manual upload) set files_uploaded=true; after cookie replacement checking the job resumes it. With no arguments, returns the map of all deployments: every deployment-enabled project with its applications and services (names, native statuses, public URLs, ports). With desk_url or project_id, returns that project's desks, images, hardware and applications; add application_id for one application. resume=false observes only. Never returns environment-variable values.

desk_url.description: Desk link from the user; selects its project for the project view.

wait_seconds.description: Wait up to this many seconds for completion; execution continues in the MCP after the response.

tools.name: sign_in
tools.description: Signs the user in to their Constructor: https://constructor.app unless url names another one (any link from it, e.g. https://acme.constructor.app). Call it when the user asks to sign in, or when a tool returns needs_auth, after telling the user a sign-in window is about to open. It opens a separate Chrome window at the sign-in page; the user signs in there and the window closes by itself. There is one sign-in at a time: signing in to another Constructor replaces it, and the MCP works there afterwards. The session is kept for this harness only, and the MCP renews it automatically for up to 14 days. Waits up to wait_seconds; while the user is still signing in it returns sign_in_pending: call it again (no second window opens), then repeat the call that needed auth.

url.description: Any link to the user's Constructor: a desk link, or just its address, e.g. https://acme.constructor.app. The user signs in there and the MCP works there afterwards, replacing any earlier sign-in. Pass it when the user names their Constructor or gives a link; omit it to sign in where the MCP works now (https://constructor.app unless the user signed in elsewhere).

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the user to finish signing in.

force.description: Open the window even though a renewable session is saved (to switch account).

tools.name: get_logs
tools.description: Last lines (default 20, up to 50) of a build or service log: why a build or start failed, how far a long build got, what a starting service prints. Constructor serves logs only live: a build log while the build runs, a service log for its current container while it runs (both replayed from the start, then streamed). The MCP follows the builds and services it starts or shows and keeps their last 50 lines, so they stay readable after the build ends or the container restarts; anything else can be read only while it runs. When a new container starts, the lines of the one before stay, above a '--- new container' marker, and restarts_seen counts them: that answers whether a service keeps restarting and why. An empty service log on a running service usually means a crash loop.

image_id.description: Image (build) ID: failure.image_id, or an image from get_deployment/list_images.

deployment_id.description: All builds and services this deployment started.

lines.description: How many of the last log lines to return.

instructions: Sign-in: the MCP works with one Constructor, https://constructor.app unless the user signed in to another. When the user asks to sign in, or names their Constructor or gives a link from it (e.g. https://acme.constructor.app), call sign_in with url set to that link. Where to act: ask the user for the Constructor desk link (they open the desk in the browser and copy the address; it contains /projects/<project>/desks/<desk>) and pass it as desk_url. Do not pick a project or desk yourself; if the user has not said where to deploy or where files live, ask. Ask the user only before replacing, renaming or deleting files on a disk, once per request for the whole list (the tools return confirm_required); creating folders and uploading new files need no question. Dockerfile rules: one Dockerfile per service named Dockerfile or <name>.dockerfile; docker-compose is not supported. The Dockerfile must build everything itself; no separate setup script the user runs before the build. The app listens on 0.0.0.0 on a fixed port; only one port per service can be public. Services reach each other through internal references (bare host:port by default, http:// only when scheme is set), never localhost; do not bake compose-style fallback hosts (http://db:5432) into ENV. Files uploaded to a desk lose the executable bit: RUN chmod 0755 any entrypoint script you COPY. In nginx configs use only the IPv4 listen line. A volume belongs to one service; services cannot share a volume. Volume data survives restarts and image changes but is wiped if the service is deleted or the volume is removed or changed. The build context is the folder containing the Dockerfile, exactly like a local docker build in that folder. Test the image locally (docker build/run) before uploading. For a local app, pass build.local_path (the folder with the Dockerfile) and deploy_app uploads it first. Hardware: leave it out; the default is used. Set hardware minimums only when the app cannot run without a GPU or a lot of RAM. Use deploy_app/update_app once for the WHOLE application. The MCP builds, resolves service URLs, configures and starts services in the background. IDs are automatic. To wait, call get_deployment(wait_seconds=20) again as often as needed (a loop of such calls is fine); never perform the deployment steps yourself. When the user asks to deploy or build, wait until the deployment is finished before answering, then give the public URL or what failed. On failure, tell the user the failed stage/service; failure.log_tail and get_logs show the last build or service log lines. Do not use browser or debugging tools. For source files: sync_files to the desk before building (the MCP checks each Dockerfile on the disk and reports warnings); after a needs_upload pause, sync and call get_deployment with files_uploaded=true. Started is not readiness.
